note: nachalei veliyya'al parallels 'breakers of death'; beliyya'al here denotes destruction/ruin (the underworld) rather than wicked people.
chevlei she'ol: chevel can mean 'pangs' or 'cords', and the parallel 'snares of death' favours 'cords'. Sheol is the realm of the dead, not hell as a place of punishment.

kjv: the snares of death prevented me (David)
mine: the snares of death confronted me (David)
note: qiddemuni means 'came to meet me, confronted me'; 'prevented' in 1611 meant 'came before', not 'stopped'. Same in 22:19.
tittappal (from patal 'twist') means God outmanoeuvres the crooked; 'unsavoury' now suggests something distasteful or disreputable.

kjv: a bow of steel is broken by mine (David's) arms
mine: my (David's) arms can bend a bow of bronze
note: qeshet nechushah is a bow of bronze (steel was unknown), and nichat means 'press down, bend (to string)', not 'break'.

kjv: thy (Yahweh's) gentleness hath made me (David) great
mine: Your (Yahweh's) answering has made me (David) great
note: 2 Sam reads 'anotekha ('your answering/help'); the KJV gives the sense of 'anwatkha 'your humility/gentleness' from the parallel Ps 18:35.

kjv: given me (David) the necks of mine enemies
mine: made my (David's) enemies turn their backs to me
note: natattah li oref means 'you gave me (their) back of the neck', i.e. made them turn and flee; 'necks' is too literal for a modern reader.

kjv: they (the foreigners) shall be afraid out of their close places
mine: came limping out of their (the foreigners') strongholds
note: yachgeru (cf. Ps 18 yachregu) is rare, probably 'limp/come out haltingly'; misgerot are fortified places.
